priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v30 REJECT, whose SHOULD-FIX named the uneven demotion of runtimeContinuity; that is repaired here exactly, with the precedence sentence in the form I named. I also accepted the subject-narrowing route at v29 that Codex subsequently rejected at v30 as insufficient for DR-126. Codex was right that a disclosure-only cell does not discharge the register row's negative-test requirement. The blocker below is not a defence of my earlier position: it is that the replacement offered for that disclosure does not close the gap either, and removes the honesty that made the previous state defensible.

blockers.appliesTo: PTCB-V30-B1 — answered by making NT-TCB-KEXEC fail-closed on NT_GNU_BUILD_ID equality and deleting the predecessor's disclosure
blockers.title: NT-TCB-KEXEC rests entirely on an identifier the executing kernel reports about itself, so a substituted kernel passes the cell, and every sentence disclosing that the gap was open has been removed
blockers.theMechanism: currentExecution.gnuBuildId is specified as 'read the NT_GNU_BUILD_ID note of the executing kernel from /sys/kernel/notes ... MUST equal authenticatedKernelMember.gnuBuildId. Absent file, unparsable notes, or mismatch refuses.' That file exposes the notes section of the kernel that is running, as reported by the kernel that is running. No TPM operation, no signature, no quote, and no measurement by any agent outside the kernel participates in producing it. It is a self-report by the entity whose identity is in question.
blockers.whyItIsNotFailClosed: The adversary this profile already models is one who can substitute the executing kernel after the measured boot — the same actor excludesSyntheticExtend was written to defeat and the same one PTCB-V30-B1 describes as having 'a different kernel enter'. An actor who can place kernel M in execution can equally cause M to carry or report the build-id of K: the note is ordinary bytes in the image, chosen at build time and readable only through M itself. The cell therefore refuses an honest or accidental substitution and passes a deliberate one. As a fail-closed negative test against the modeled adversary it does no work, and NT-TCB-KEXEC is asserted as exactly that: 'This is undeclared/drifted OS ABI (NT-TCB-1/NT-TCB-3 class). Not a disclosure. Not inapplicable', with g22.doesNotClaim now reading 'NT-TCB-KEXEC is a required fail-closed cell, not a skipped disclosure.'
blockers.theContractAlreadySaysThis: This is not an outside standard I am importing. PTCB-V22-B2 rejected an earlier generation on the ground that 'NT_GNU_BUILD_ID equality is not a cryptographic measurement of the executing kernel bytes', and that finding is still recorded in this artifact's own honestyRepairs. The live text still carries the rule at runningKernelImagePath: 'Filename/osrelease and executingKernelBuildId MUST NOT establish authenticity.' And the linux-pathless tag's own forbidden list still contains 'executingKernelBuildId' — unqualified, unlike the neighbouring 'ima-kernel-image as authenticity bind' — while currentExecution.gnuBuildId, the same datum, is now required: true on that same tag. The role labels ('not a second authenticity digest and not IMA') separate intent from the authenticity path, which I credit, but they do not change what the datum can demonstrate, and NT-TCB-KEXEC is a security test, not a bookkeeping field.
blockers.theRemovedDisclosure: v30 stated the limitation in five places. All five are gone in v31, and I verified each by substring count: the NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC negative-test entry (0 occurrences), the subject observation's 'not a claim that the currently executing image was never replaced after that launch' (0), inScopeBootConfigs' 'It does not authenticate a later kexec or other post-boot kernel replacement' (0), unavailableRefuses' 'This refusal set does not claim to detect post-boot kexec' (0), and whatThisDoesNotDo's 'Does not claim the currently executing kernel equals the firmware-launched kernel after a post-boot kexec or similar replacement' (0). g22.doesNotClaim's kexec limitation sentence was replaced by the fail-closed assertion. The net movement is that a true statement of a known limit was deleted and an untrue statement of closure put in its place, which is a regression in honesty even though the artifact reads stronger.
blockers.failureScenario: An in-scope machine boots kernel K under Secure Boot; the signed transcript, the boot-manager handoff, the composite quote and the PE/COFF image-digest equality all verify, so firmware-launched-kernel-package authenticity holds and I do not dispute it. The privileged OS-time actor then enters kernel M, built from a different source revision but carrying K's NT_GNU_BUILD_ID note, or patched so that /sys/kernel/notes emits it. At qualification the verifier reads /sys/kernel/notes, obtains K's build-id, compares it to authenticatedKernelMember.gnuBuildId, and the values are equal. NT-TCB-KEXEC passes. refusesBootConfigs' 'A different executing kernel (build-id mismatch or absent notes) refuses' does not fire, because there is no mismatch to observe. The DR-126 negative-test matrix records a satisfied fail-closed cell for a machine whose executing OS ABI is not the allowlisted one, and no clause anywhere now discloses that this outcome is possible.
blockers.severityRationale: This yields a positive assurance — a passing required cell in the register row's negative-test matrix — on a machine where the property under test is false, and it removes the disclosure that previously kept the same underlying gap honest. That is the class this row has consistently rated as a blocker. It is not a determinacy or over-refusal defect.
blockers.requiredRepair: Two honest routes, matching the two Codex named at v30. (1) Meet the requirement properly: bind the executing kernel through evidence rooted outside the kernel being examined — a runtime measurement or appraisal anchored in the TPM or in firmware, or an enforced non-replacement property established before any replacement can be staged and carried monotonically to observedAt — and only then describe NT-TCB-KEXEC as fail-closed. (2) If no such mechanism is available this generation, restore the v30 disclosures verbatim and keep the build-id comparison, but characterise it accurately: a drift detector that catches an honest or accidental substitution and cannot detect a deliberate one, recorded as a non-closing cell with the limitation visible at NT-TCB-1 and g22 exactly as v30 had it. Under either route, reconcile the linux-pathless forbidden list with currentExecution so the same datum is not simultaneously forbidden and required on one tag. Everything else in this generation should be kept verbatim.

repairsVerified.finding: CLAUDE-V30-S1 (mine) — runtimeContinuity demoted in two clauses and not in six others
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED exactly, and with the precedence sentence in the form I specified. A new roleGoverns field reads 'runtimeContinuity.role is the governing sentence for this field, in the same form as authenticatedManifest.uniqueness and peCoffImageDigestAlgorithm.specificationGoverns.' role now reads 'OPTIONAL HARDENING only. Not an interval proof. Not NT-TCB-KEXEC ... Absent indicators MUST NOT refuse. Only a contradictory present value may fail closed: if /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_loaded exists and equals 1, refuse.' All four indicator sentences were rewritten to match — each now says absence MUST NOT refuse — and both stale statements I named are fixed: enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity now reads 'OPTIONAL HARDENING. roleGoverns. Not the post-boot interval constraint. Absent indicators MUST NOT refuse this machine', and whatThisDoesNotDo now reads 'Does not treat runtimeContinuity as an interval proof or as NT-TCB-KEXEC. roleGoverns.' The kexec-enabled-machines line is gone. The machine I described — replacement support compiled out, transcript matching — now qualifies under every clause, which resolves the divergence.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-B2 — measuredBootTranscript called signed with no location or join in the signed-carrier schema
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. The PATHLESS signedObject now carries measuredBootTranscriptDigest, 'required on Linux OS ABI; forbidden on macOS', as the 64-hex sha-256 of measuredBootTranscriptCanonical, with both platform shapes closed exactly: 'Linux signedObject is exactly {tag, pathlessObservation, measuredBootTranscriptDigest}' and 'macOS signedObject is exactly {tag, pathlessObservation}', both extrasRejected. measuredBootBind carries the matching reference requiring equality to 'the signed PATHLESS measuredBootTranscriptDigest for this platformProfileKey and OS-ABI signed entry', with 'Unknown, extra, or cross-entry transcript refuses', which is the uniqueness and cross-entry substitution refusal Codex required.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-S2 — preferred RPM extraction still named the closed snapFd
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. preferredApi.extract.on is now 'roFd after verify and lseek 0. snapFd is closed and MUST NOT be named here.' Extraction also gained completeness rules — walk every member until the end iterator, any short read or error refuses.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-S3 — recomputeDigest not wired into preKernelReferences and input bytes not retained
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. preKernelReferences.join now requires 'recomputedDigest MUST equal event.digests[TPM_ALG_SHA256] and the transcript row digestSha256', adds 'Do not call eventPreimage(event)', and keeps the tagged signedEntry equalities. Each recomputeDigest type family gained a retained field naming the canonical preimage bytes to keep.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-S4 — ACTION and VARIABLE preimages did not reproduce the TCG event bytes
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, and this corrects a real error I did not catch at v30. EV_EFI_ACTION is now 'an 8-bit (not UCS-2) action string of EventSize bytes, including any specified terminator' against the pinned PFP — the v30 text said UCS-2-LE, which would not reproduce the logged digest. UEFI_VARIABLE_DATA is now serialized field-by-field: 'UEFI_GUID (16 bytes) || UINT64 UnicodeNameLength (little-endian) || UINT64 VariableDataLength (little-endian) || CHAR16 UnicodeName[...] || INT8 VariableData[...]', with the explicit 'Not UnicodeName||VariableData alone', which was precisely the v30 defect.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-S5 — skipping every EV_NO_ACTION omitted StartupLocality replay semantics
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. replayAlgorithm.init now distinguishes the two cases: PCRs 1, 2, 4 and 7 initialize to 32 zero bytes, while PCR 0 takes 'the PFP locality-dependent startup value for that locality byte' when the log contains the defined StartupLocality EV_NO_ACTION, with that row explicitly not extended, and otherwise initializes to zeros.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-S6 — no transcript row for the PCR-7 facts establishing Secure Boot trust
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. The transcript now covers 'every PCR-0/1/2/4/7 event from the start of the log through the first EV_SEPARATOR on that same PCR inclusive', with 'PCR-7 SecureBoot/PK/KEK/db/dbx rows used as security facts MUST appear', so the PCR-7 metadata is type-and-order authenticated by the same signed transcript before use, and the corrected VARIABLE serialization applies to it.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V30-B1 — a disclosure-only non-test cannot substitute for the required host-ABI negative test
repairsVerified.result: NOT REPAIRED — see CLAUDE-V31-B1. I agree with Codex that a disclosure-only cell does not discharge DR-126's negative-test requirement. The substitute offered is not one of the two remedies Codex specified: it neither authenticates the currently executing kernel nor enforces that replacement cannot occur, and it deletes the disclosure that made the open state honest.

limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed the eight claimed repairs against all eight predecessor findings, the new currentExecution and transcript surfaces, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness. CLAUDE-V31-B1 rests on what /sys/kernel/notes is — a section of the running kernel image surfaced by that same kernel — and on this contract's own recorded reasoning about NT_GNU_BUILD_ID, not on execution against a live machine. Route (2) of the repair requires conceding nothing technical, since it only restores statements this artifact carried one generation ago.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at f410ef1a... and 0444 at both ends, HEAD steady, 43/43 chain pins reproduce, both frozen v30 verdicts reproduce with no replacement, 55 changed paths with zero off-roster, reviewGuidance a pure append, Linux still in D-002 slice 1, all 26 D-096 mentions refusals. Seven findings are repaired and several are exemplary. My own SHOULD-FIX is closed with the precedence sentence in the exact form I named, all four indicators rewritten so absence cannot refuse, and both stale statements corrected. The signed transcript now has a real home in a closed per-platform signedObject with cross-entry substitution refusal; the transcript covers PCR 7 so the Secure Boot facts are type-and-order authenticated before use; replay distinguishes StartupLocality and takes the locality-dependent PCR 0 initial value; recomputeDigest is wired into preKernelReferences with the legacy call forbidden; extraction is confined to roFd with completeness rules; and the ACTION and VARIABLE preimages are corrected — the action string is 8-bit rather than UCS-2 and UEFI_VARIABLE_DATA now carries the GUID and both little-endian lengths, which is a real error in the predecessor that I had not caught. The eighth is the problem. Codex was right at v30 that a disclosure-only cell does not discharge DR-126's negative-test requirement, but the substitute is not one of the two remedies Codex specified. NT-TCB-KEXEC is now fail-closed on currentExecution.gnuBuildId, read from /sys/kernel/notes — the notes section of the running kernel, surfaced by that same running kernel, with no TPM, signature, quote or external measurement involved. An actor who can put a different kernel into execution can equally have it carry or report the expected build-id, so the cell refuses an honest substitution and passes a deliberate one. This contract established that reasoning at v22, still records it in its own honestyRepairs, still states at runningKernelImagePath that executingKernelBuildId MUST NOT establish authenticity, and still lists executingKernelBuildId unqualified in the very tag where the same datum is now required. Compounding it, all five sentences in which v30 disclosed that the gap was open now measure zero occurrences, and g22.doesNotClaim asserts closure in their place. The net effect is that a true statement of a limit was deleted and an untrue statement of closure installed, producing a passing required cell in the register row's negative-test matrix for a machine whose executing OS ABI is not the allowlisted one. Either root the executing-kernel evidence outside the kernel being examined, or restore the v30 disclosures and describe the build-id comparison as the drift detector it is.
